facts.raw_span: slowly growing subcutaneous node in the right axilla
progressive infiltration of the overlying skin over the past year
swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy over 20 years ago
mild episodic pain in her right axilla during menstrual cycles
Solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque in the right axilla measuring 5 × 3 cm
Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement
Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm
Positive for: pancytokeratin (AE1/AE3), cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies
Negative for: synaptophysin, chromogranin, and S100-stainings
Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration
1 of the sentinel lymph nodes showed isolated cytokeratin8/18–positive tumor cells and MNF116-positive tumor cells
Chest, abdominal, and pelvic CT scans, cranial and breast MRI, mammography, and breast sonography revealed no evidence of primary or secondary tumors

concepts.why: The presence of dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat, tumor cells in an 'Indian file pattern', and positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies support this diagnosis.
The solitary, indolent, erythematous plaque and positive immunohistochemistry for cytokeratin 20 and GATA3 antibodies are consistent with this diagnosis.
The dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat and tumor cells in an 'Indian file pattern' are consistent with this diagnosis, although the immunohistochemistry profile is not entirely specific.

The presence of cytokeratin8/18–positive and MNF116-positive tumor cells in a sentinel lymph node and the patient's history of swelling in the right axilla during pregnancy suggest a possible breast origin, although the primary tumor was not detected.

rationales.F06: Dermal tumor infiltrating the subcutaneous fat without epidermal involvement is characteristic of cutaneous apocrine carcinoma and hidradenocarcinoma.
rationales.F07: Tumor cells diffusely dispersed between collagen bundles and lined up in an 'Indian file pattern' with basophilic nuclei and scant cytoplasm is characteristic of cutaneous apocrine carcinoma and hidradenocarcinoma.
rationales.F08: Positive immunohistochemistry for pancytokeratin, cytokeratin 20, GCDFP15, estrogen receptor, and GATA3 antibodies is characteristic of cutaneous apocrine carcinoma and metastatic breast carcinoma.
rationales.F10: Multiple GATA3-positive and estrogen receptor–positive apocrine glands in close association to diffuse tumor cell infiltration is characteristic of cutaneous apocrine carcinoma.
rationales.F12: No evidence of primary or secondary tumors on imaging studies makes metastatic breast carcinoma less likely.
